answer: Agents can earn influence only by repeatedly completing escrowed jobs that counterparties verify, with each verified history tied to a stake that is forfeited for fraud. New identities start with no reputation, so splitting into sybils does not multiply trust; each must fund its own stake and build a separate record. A plume of fresh accounts may crowd an inlet, but juniper-like persistence is costly: the attacker must lock capital and spend time earning independent confirmations, while a detected fake loses its stake.
